brief.title: Teacher dashboard for state assessment programme
business_goals: Teachers can see their own class's foundational literacy and numeracy scores after each assessment cycle, in the language they teach in.
Teachers can see which specific learning outcomes their students are struggling with, broken down by competency.
Teachers are provided with suggested remedial activities for each weak competency, pulled from the existing worksheet library.
Block education officers can see average scores across all schools in their block to identify schools needing support.
The department can track cohort progress over a child's schooling using historical assessment data.

stakeholders.name: Anita Deshmukh
concerns: Rolling out to about 12,000 government primary school teachers across the state.
Teachers need to see class scores and competency breakdown in their teaching language.
Dashboard must work in Hindi, Marathi, and English at minimum for this phase.
Strict access control for student data to prevent issues with parents.
Must be ready before the next assessment cycle starts in June (immovable deadline).

stakeholders.name: Rohan Bhatt
concerns: Teachers have only basic smartphones and unreliable data connectivity.
Dashboard must load in under 5 seconds on a 3G connection.
Dashboard should suggest remedial activities for weak competencies.
Individual student scores should only be visible to that student's own teacher and their block officer (data privacy).

stakeholders.name: Kavita Suresh
concerns: Dashboard needs to pull scanned assessment results from the existing OMR scanning system.
The OMR scanning process is not changing.
Block education officers need a rollup view of average scores across schools.
Dashboard must be read-only for teachers; no editing or overriding scores.

stakeholders.name: Imran Sheikh
concerns: Handling data volume of about 3.5 million individual student assessment records per cycle, four cycles a year.
Dashboard queries need to stay responsive as historical data builds up.
At least three years of historical assessment data must be retained.

constraints: Target audience of 12,000 government primary school teachers.
Teachers use basic smartphones and have unreliable data connectivity.
Dashboard must load in under 5 seconds on a 3G connection.
Must integrate with and pull data from the existing OMR scanning system.
Existing OMR scanning process cannot be changed.
Must support Hindi, Marathi, and English languages at minimum for this phase.
System must handle 3.5 million individual student assessment records per cycle (four cycles a year).
Dashboard queries must remain responsive with multiple years of historical data.
Individual student scores must only be visible to that student's own teacher and their block officer (strict access control).
At least three years of historical assessment data must be retained.
Budget for this phase is fixed at 60 lakh rupees.
Must be ready before the next assessment cycle starts in June (fixed deadline).
out_of_scope: Other regional languages beyond Hindi, Marathi, and English are not in this year's scope.
Teachers will not have features to edit or override assessment scores; the dashboard is read-only for teachers.

requirements.statement: The system shall display class scores in the teacher's teaching language.
requirements.evidence: Teachers need a dashboard where they can see their own class's foundational literacy and numeracy scores after each assessment cycle, in the language they teach in.

requirements.statement: The system shall load the dashboard in under 5 seconds on a 3G connection.
requirements.evidence: The dashboard has to load in under 5 seconds on a 3G connection, or teachers just won't use it — we saw that with the last app we rolled out.

requirements.statement: The system shall pull scanned assessment results from the existing OMR scanning system.
requirements.evidence: The dashboard needs to pull scanned assessment results from the existing OMR scanning system once they're processed — we're not changing how the scanning happens.

requirements.statement: The system shall not require changes to the existing OMR scanning process.

requirements.statement: The system shall suggest remedial activities for each weak competency.
requirements.evidence: Ideally the dashboard would also suggest a remedial activity for each weak competency, pulled from the existing worksheet library, so teachers don't have to search for material themselves.

requirements.evidence: Other regional languages would be nice for later but that's not this year's scope.

requirements.statement: The system shall maintain responsive dashboard queries as historical data builds up over multiple years.

requirements.statement: The system shall provide read-only access to the dashboard for teachers.

epics.title: View Class Performance Insights
epics.goal: For teachers to understand their class's performance and identify areas of struggle.

epics.title: Access Remedial Resources
epics.goal: For teachers to find relevant support materials for their students.

epics.title: Monitor Block-Level Performance
epics.goal: For Block Education Officers to oversee educational progress in their jurisdiction.

epics.title: Ensure Data Integrity & Performance
epics.goal: To ensure the dashboard is reliable, fast, and uses accurate assessment data.

stories.title: View Class Assessment Summary
stories.i_want: to see my class's foundational literacy and numeracy scores for the latest assessment cycle
stories.so_that: I can quickly understand my class's overall performance in my teaching language.

acceptance_criteria.given: I am a Class Teacher for Grade 3, my teaching language is Hindi, and the latest assessment cycle results are available
acceptance_criteria.then: I see my Grade 3 class's average foundational literacy and numeracy scores displayed in Hindi.

acceptance_criteria.given: I am a Class Teacher for Grade 5, my teaching language is Marathi, and the latest assessment cycle results are available
acceptance_criteria.then: I see my Grade 5 class's average foundational literacy and numeracy scores displayed in Marathi.

acceptance_criteria.given: I am a Class Teacher for Grade 4, my teaching language is English, and the latest assessment cycle results are available
acceptance_criteria.then: I see my Grade 4 class's average foundational literacy and numeracy scores displayed in English.

stories.title: Identify Struggling Learning Outcomes
stories.i_want: to see which specific learning outcomes my students are struggling with, broken down by competency
stories.so_that: I can pinpoint exact areas where my class needs additional support.

acceptance_criteria.given: I am a Class Teacher viewing my class's assessment results
acceptance_criteria.when: I select a subject area like "Literacy"
acceptance_criteria.then: I see a list of competencies (e.g., "Reading Comprehension") with associated learning outcomes where my class's average score is below 60%.

acceptance_criteria.given: my class has performed well in "Number Recognition" (e.g., average score above 60%)
acceptance_criteria.then: "Number Recognition" is not highlighted as a struggling competency.

stories.title: View Suggested Remedial Activities
stories.i_want: to see suggested remedial activities for each weak competency identified in my class
stories.so_that: I can easily find and use relevant resources to help my students improve.

acceptance_criteria.given: I am a Class Teacher viewing a struggling competency like "Phonics"
acceptance_criteria.then: I see a list of suggested remedial activities pulled from the existing worksheet library.

acceptance_criteria.given: the worksheet library is temporarily unavailable
acceptance_criteria.when: I try to view remedial activities for a competency
acceptance_criteria.then: the system displays a message indicating that remedial activities are currently unavailable.

stories.title: View Block-Level Assessment Averages
stories.i_want: to see average foundational literacy and numeracy scores across all schools in my block
stories.so_that: I can identify schools that may need additional support or intervention.

acceptance_criteria.given: I am a Block Education Officer for Block A
acceptance_criteria.then: I see the average foundational literacy and numeracy scores for all schools within Block A, clearly aggregated.

acceptance_criteria.given: I am a Block Education Officer for Block A
acceptance_criteria.when: I attempt to access assessment data for Block B
acceptance_criteria.then: the system displays only data pertaining to Block A.

stories.title: Secure Teacher's Class Data
stories.i_want: to ensure only I can see my students' individual assessment scores
stories.so_that: my students' privacy is protected and other teachers cannot access their detailed performance data.

acceptance_criteria.given: I am a Class Teacher for Grade 3
acceptance_criteria.when: Another teacher from my school attempts to view individual student scores from my Grade 3 class
acceptance_criteria.then: The system displays an access denied message or hides the individual student scores from them.

acceptance_criteria.given: I am a Class Teacher for Grade 3
acceptance_criteria.when: I access my dashboard to view my class's detailed assessment data
acceptance_criteria.then: I can see the individual student scores for students in my Grade 3 class.

stories.title: Access Individual Student Scores for Block
stories.i_want: to view individual student assessment scores for students within my block
stories.so_that: I can identify specific students or schools needing targeted support.

acceptance_criteria.given: I am a Block Education Officer for Block A
acceptance_criteria.when: I access the dashboard and navigate to a school within Block A
acceptance_criteria.then: the dashboard displays individual student assessment scores for students enrolled in that school.

acceptance_criteria.given: I am a Block Education Officer for Block A
acceptance_criteria.when: I attempt to view individual student scores for a student in Block B
acceptance_criteria.then: The system displays an access denied message or hides the individual student scores from Block B.

issues: The acceptance criteria define 'struggling' with a hardcoded 60% threshold (AC1, AC2). Requirement R-006 does not specify this threshold, making the story less negotiable and prescribing an implementation detail. The ACs test a specific implementation choice rather than the requirement itself in a negotiable way.
reviews.fix_instructions: Remove the specific '60%' threshold from AC1 and AC2. Instead, the ACs should refer to a system-defined or configurable threshold for 'struggling' outcomes, e.g., 'where my class's average score is below the defined threshold for struggling competencies.'

gaps.description: The business goal for the department to track cohort progress over a child's schooling using historical assessment data (Goal 5) is not explicitly addressed by any requirement or story. While data retention (R-020) and responsive queries (R-014) are covered, there's no feature for viewing or analyzing this cohort progress.
gaps.suggested_question: We have requirements for retaining historical data, but no specific features for the department to actually *track cohort progress* over time. What specific views or reports are needed for this goal?

gaps.description: While specific access control rules for student data are defined (R-017, R-018, R-019), there are no broader non-functional requirements for general system security, such as data encryption (at rest or in transit), protection against common web vulnerabilities, or a security audit process. Given the sensitive nature of student data and the scale, this is a critical omission.
gaps.suggested_question: Beyond the specific access rules for teachers and block officers, what are the overall security requirements for the system, such as data encryption, vulnerability testing, or incident response?

gaps.description: Requirement R-009 states that block education officers can see 'average scores.' The specific calculation method for these averages (e.g., mean, median, weighted average, how to handle missing data) is not defined, which could lead to different interpretations and inconsistent reporting.
gaps.suggested_question: For the 'average scores' displayed to block education officers (R-009), how exactly should these averages be calculated? For example, should it be a simple mean, a weighted average, or something else?

gaps.description: The project involves rolling out a dashboard to 12,000 teachers using basic smartphones with unreliable connectivity. There is no identified stakeholder or requirements addressing the needs of a support or helpdesk team who would assist these teachers with technical issues, password resets, or data inquiries.
related_ids: Constraint: Target audience of 12,000 government primary school teachers
gaps.suggested_question: With 12,000 teachers using the system, who will be responsible for providing technical support, and what tools or features will they need to assist users effectively?

gaps.coverage_note: The backlog provides good coverage for the core functional requirements related to teachers viewing class scores, struggling outcomes, and remedial activities, as well as block officers viewing averages. Key non-functional aspects like performance, language support, and data integration are also addressed. However, there are some significant gaps, particularly around a key business goal for the department to track cohort progress, broader system security beyond access control, and the operational needs for supporting a large user base. Clarifying the calculation of 'average scores' is also important for accurate reporting.
